problems.title: The printed accounting interface returns zero after positive call paths
problems.source_location: Current proceedings Appendix E, PDF pp.21–22, generated-method listing lines 95–148; comparison arXiv v1 corresponding author listing
claim: The provided case-generation example returns fields for LLM calls, input/output tokens and token cost, but initializes all of them to zero after its generation activity.
analysis: A positive-call helper invokes the client, while the unconditional return block still reports \((N_{\rm calls},N_{\rm in},N_{\rm out})=(0,0,0)\). For any execution making at least one counted call, the reported call count is therefore false. This follows statically without creating an attack or contacting a model.

An external wrapper could maintain an independent ledger and ignore these fields. Current author-repository metadata is inaccessible, so this check concerns the author’s printed example, not an obtained full orchestration implementation. No trace establishes that the reported query-reduction tables used this dictionary.
result: The example’s accounting interface cannot substantiate cost on positive-call paths; no corrected historical query count is inferred.
problems.impact_rationale: The local author-example accounting defect is direct, but the central reported reduction is not linked to that return field by available run evidence.
repair: The supplied correction records counted events at the client boundary and returns before/after ledger differences, with explicit retry/cache and billing conventions. No attack-generation modification or execution is needed.
problems.existing_correction_status: The existing correction is retained as a bounded proposal; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The table’s comparison and cost claim needs an explicit scope
problems.source_location: Current proceedings Table 2, PDF p.7; Appendix D Table 5, p.18
claim: The table caption describes uniformly higher success at lower cost; the actual comparisons depend on target, comparator, resource unit and amortized setup.
analysis: On GPT-4o the displayed ASRs are \(0.69\) versus AutoDAN-Turbo’s \(0.76\); on Mixtral both are \(0.96\). AutoRedTeamer exceeds PAIR and TAP across the four targets. Lower evaluation-call counts, amortized setup, token expenditure and latency are different comparisons. For example, fixed setup and per-case Llama counts against Rainbow give \(82+14N\) versus \(6000+4N\), crossing at \(N=591.8\). This is a conditional accounting illustration, not a recovered billing trace.
result: Retain the favorable comparisons actually supported by the table and qualify universal caption language. No separate empirical score defect is established.
problems.impact_rationale: The table itself permits a narrower accurate comparison; this caption/accounting scope clarification is not counted as an additional scientific error.
problems.existing_correction_status: Retain a scoped comparison statement; no paper repair or recomputed ASR is asserted.
